subject: Post-demo: VertexAI comparison & 1M-token econ asks
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice@vertexai.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + quick econ asks

Hi Alice — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and a few asks so we can align on the competitive claims you heard from the hyperscaler team.

Summary from our side: the demo showed standard chat flows (user prompt -> model context ~1.2k tokens, response ~180 tokens). You mentioned the hyperscaler told you they can beat our per-1M token economics by ~30% if you run on their managed endpoint. Before we dive into procurement, we want to validate that comparison across realistic knobs: batching, prefix/KV cache hit rate, and quantization.

What we attached: Redwood_TCO_v2.xlsx (estimates based on your demo prompts) and a small CSV with our 1M-token calc. In short:
- Redwood hosted baseline (no cache, sample model FP16): ~$9.8 per 1M tokens for this workload
- With realistic caching (we see 50–75% prefix reuse for conversational flows) + batching (batch=16) + our optimized kernels -> effective $3.1–$4.0 per 1M tokens depending on hit rate and quantization.

Requests from you (to confirm):
1) Can you share the hyperscaler quote/email that states their 30% gap? we want the exact config (model size, quantization, expected concurrency).
2) Are you open to a short benchmark where we run your production prompts (1M tokens total) against: batch sizes [8,16,32], cache hit targets [0,50,70,90] and two model variants (quantized and FP16)?

Proposed next steps:
- If yes, we run a controlled 1M-token benchmark and provide: per-1M token $ estimate, p50/p95 latency for each config, and the split of token cost (compute vs overhead).
- If procurement needs numbers for the SOW, we can provide a short snapshot for the initial commit (RDW-2319).

Ben/Marcus — can you both review the attached calc and prep the bench template if Alice agrees? I'd like to offer a 48–72 hour turnaround for the benchmark if we can get the prompts.

Thanks,
Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Alice Moreno <alice@vertexai.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@vertexai.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + quick econ asks

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: the hyperscaler comparison came from their solution architect, and they assumed a large LLM (70B-equivalent), 8-bit quant, and batch=32 for steady-state throughput. Their emailed claim was a ~28–35% lower unit cost for the same throughput under a 0% cache assumption. I can forward the thread — procurement is on copy.

We are definitely open to the benchmark you suggested. A couple of asks:
- We want the benchmark to use our top 150 production prompts (I can provide them as a CSV).
- Can Redwood run the test in our us-west region and mirror our concurrency (we expect 120 concurrent sessions at peak)?
- Please include tail-latency (p95/p99) since our UX team is sensitive to spikes.

I can share the prompt set and the hyperscaler email by EOD Monday. Please confirm the test matrix and what you need from procurement for an NDA/benchmark agreement.

Best,
Alice
Director, Platform Engineering — VertexAI
alice@vertexai.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 18:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo recap + quick econ asks (bench plan + calc)

Rishi / Marcus — I reviewed the attached Redwood_TCO_v2.xlsx and updated 1M_token_calc.csv (attached). High level plan for the benchmark if Alice sends the prompts:

Test matrix (run for 1M tokens each row):
- Batch size: 8, 16, 32
- Cache hit rate: 0%, 50%, 70%, 90% (we will implement prefix/KV cache replay to simulate hits)
- Model variant: FP16 (baseline), 8-bit quant (our quantized path)
- Concurrency: single-connection and 120 concurrent sessions (to capture throughput/latency tradeoffs)

Metrics we will capture:
- Tokens generated (total), tokens served from cache, cache hit ratio
- Effective per-1M token compute cost (GPU runtime * $/GPU-hour breakdown)
- End-to-end p50/p95/p99 latency and tail-units lost to queueing or batching delay
- Batch fill efficiency (avg batch size)

Preliminary numbers (from lab runs with similar prompts):
- Batch=16 + 70% cache + 8-bit: ~$2.9 per 1M tokens, p95 ~180ms
- Batch=32 + 0% cache + FP16: ~$6.6 per 1M tokens, p95 ~240ms

Action items and owners:
- Rishi: collect Vertex prompt CSV and hyperscaler quote (Alice to send) — due Mon EOD
- Marcus: prep benchmark harness + infra recipe (Docker image, workload runner) and add a warmup plan — due Tue noon
- Ben: run cost calc and prepare a short 1‑pager comparing Redwood vs hyperscaler assumptions we'll share with procurement — due Wed EOD

Attachments: 1M_token_calc.csv (contains our token math and GPU-hour assumptions).

I recommend we offer Vertex a quick 48–72 hour SLA for the benchmark once the prompts land — fast turnaround usually helps clarify the economics.

-ben

--
Ben Carter
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
